## Background

You're a junior data analyst at a healthcare system. Department leadership has asked your team for an analysis of **trends in HbA1c control at four clinics** — is control improving, holding steady, or slipping, clinic by clinic?

Your data engineer pulled the data, and — kind of lazily — handed you **three separate files** instead of one clean extract:

-   `encounters.csv` — one row per patient encounter, but instead of the clinic name it only lists `provider_id` (apparently linking encounters to clinics was somebody else's job)
-   `labs.csv` — one row per lab result
-   `provider_lookup.csv` — the file that actually maps each `provider_id` to a clinic, which someone should have joined in before handing this to you

Before you got to the data, your senior colleague started this document to lay out what's needed — but only got as far as comments. The code is yours to write. Today you'll get **Clinics A and C** done; the other two are this week's homework.

## What "in control" means here

> **Denominator (per clinic, per month):** number of distinct patients with at least one encounter at that clinic that month.
>
> **Numerator (per clinic, per month):** of those, how many have an `HbA1c` lab result recorded **that same month** below 8%. A patient with no HbA1c result that month does not count — a missing test isn't the same as good control.

These files are not clean. Budget real time for step 2.

glimpse(encounters)
glimpse(labs)
